BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

title: Simplify AtomicFileWriter and use clearer temporary file names

=========== administrativemonitor-at-since.yaml ===========
title: Add missing at-since in AdministrativeMonitor
category: feature
requirement: '## Context


  The AdministrativeMonitor API recently gained manager-aware permission helpers, but its Javadoc still does not say which Jenkins version introduced them.


  ## Desired outcome


  The API documentation should identify the correct release so plugin developers can make versioned compatibility decisions.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The behavior of administrative monitors is unchanged, but the new monitor permission helpers have explicit `@since` metadata.

  '
=========== agent-protocols-config-removal.yaml ===========
title: Removing configurability of `Jenkins.agentProtocols`
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator should not have to manually curate the list of built-in inbound agent protocols in the global security screen, because that configuration can drift away from the supported transport set and create confusion about what Jenkins actually allows.


  ## Desired outcome

  Jenkins should stop treating built-in agent protocols as an administrator-managed security setting and should instead expose the supported protocol set directly from core. The configuration UI and backing APIs should no longer offer agent protocol toggles that imply these built-in transports can be selectively disabled there.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The global security configuration no longer presents agent protocol selection as an editable admin setting, Jenkins reports the supported built-in protocols from core without relying on saved UI state, and upgrading preserves working agent connectivity without a manual protocol reconfiguration step.

  '
=========== atomicfilewriter-temp-names.yaml ===========
title: Simplify AtomicFileWriter and use clearer temporary file names
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins operator writing critical configuration files expects atomic writes to stay dependable and the resulting logs to be readable when the filesystem does not support true atomic moves, but the current implementation produces obscure temporary names and noisy duplicate failure reporting.


  ## Desired outcome

  `AtomicFileWriter` should create clearer temporary file names derived from the destination path and should remember after the first `AtomicMoveNotSupportedException` that the platform requires a non-atomic fallback. Once that fallback is known, Jenkins should replace the target cleanly without repeating the unsupported atomic attempt on every write.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Temporary files are easier to identify from their names, the first unsupported atomic move downgrades subsequent writes to the non-atomic replacement path, and operators no longer see duplicate stack traces caused by retry-and-rethrow logic when the filesystem lacks atomic move support.

  '
=========== autocomplete-query-parameters.yaml ===========
title: '[JENKINS-37241] Support for query parameters in autocomplete'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator or plugin author exposing an autocomplete field may need extra query parameters to scope the results, but the current autocomplete widget only sends the search term and makes it impossible to express that richer filtering contract.


  ## Desired outcome

  Autocomplete endpoints should be able to declare additional query parameters through the descriptor contract, and the browser widget should include them when fetching suggestions. This should let server-side autocomplete logic honor contextual filters without changing the visible widget behavior for fields that do not need extra parameters.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Autocomplete requests include any descriptor-defined extra query parameters alongside the typed term, existing fields without extra parameters keep working as before, and filtered suggestion endpoints can finally distinguish context that was previously unavailable to them.

  '
=========== autocomplete-suggestion-count.yaml ===========
title: Allow plugins to customize number of suggestions in autocomplete
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  Some plugins need far more or far fewer autocomplete suggestions than Jenkins’s hard-coded default, but today they cannot express that preference in the rendered control.


  ## Desired outcome


  Plugin authors should be able to set the maximum suggestion count per autocomplete field without forking the widget.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The widget still defaults to 10 suggestions when nothing is specified, but a field can override that limit through the `data-maxsuggestions` attribute.

  '
=========== background-discarder-logging.yaml ===========
title: '[JENKINS-73692] Turn off logging from `BackgroundGlobalBuildDiscarder`'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context


  Background global build discarder maintenance can produce noisy per-job logging even when it is working normally, which makes administrative logs harder to scan.


  ## Desired outcome


  Keep the discarder behavior the same while removing routine chatter from its listener output.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The build discarder still evaluates jobs and applies matching retention strategies, but it no longer prints per-job progress lines for every processed job.

  '
=========== backport-24622-ui-fixes.yaml ===========
title: Backporting for 2.462.2
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  The 2.462.2 stabilization work included frontend fixes for add-item layouts, and users on the maintained line need the same polish instead of a visually inconsistent form experience.


  ## Desired outcome


  Backport the UI fixes so adding configurable blocks in Jenkins forms uses the corrected spacing and table styling from the stabilized release line.


  ## Acceptance signals


  Newly added items use the backported layout behavior instead of the older broken presentation, and the change stays confined to the front-end rendering of the add-item workflow.

=========== boot-version-logging.yaml ===========
title: Print Jenkins version on boot
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins operator starting or upgrading a controller often needs to confirm from the startup logs exactly which Jenkins version is coming up, but boot logs do not currently state that version explicitly.


  ## Desired outcome

  When Jenkins starts, the normal startup log should include the controller version so administrators can confirm the running build without inferring it from package metadata or the UI. The boot message should clearly report the value returned by `Jenkins.getVersion()`.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Startup logs include a message containing the current Jenkins version during initialization, operators can confirm the running version from boot output alone, and no extra manual step is required to verify which release started.

  '

category: other
requirement: '## Context

  ## Desired outcome

  Attempts to delete a running build must fail cleanly instead of partially removing it, with the user-visible message `Unable to delete <job> #<build> because it is still running`.   ## Acceptance signals

  ## Desired outcome

  ## Acceptance signals


  The widget refreshes on window focus, updates while viewing older pages, and preserves the current pagination context when reloading the build list.

  ## Desired outcome

  ## Acceptance signals

category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  ## Desired outcome

  ## Acceptance signals

  ## Desired outcome

title: Fix error message when creation of item by type is prohibited
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context


  When Jenkins blocks creation of an item or view type for permission reasons, the error message includes a malformed permission path that repeats internal permission text and confuses administrators.


  ## Desired outcome

  ## Acceptance signals

  '
=========== item-deletion-preflight-hook.yaml ===========
title: '`ItemListener.onCheckDelete` & `ItemDeletion.cancelBuildsInProgress`'
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  Plugins sometimes need to veto deletion before Jenkins starts canceling queue items or interrupting running builds, but the current deletion flow does not offer a dedicated preflight hook.


  ## Desired outcome


  Item deletion should expose a pre-delete extension point and centralize the logic that cancels in-flight work, while keeping the observable deletion safeguards the same.


  ## Acceptance signals


  `ItemListener.onCheckDelete(Item)` runs before deletion work starts and can stop the operation, `ItemDeletion.cancelBuildsInProgress` owns the build-cancellation behavior, and users still see the same protection against deleting items with builds that cannot be stopped cleanly.

  '
=========== javadoc-api-version-markers.yaml ===========
title: Update version numbers of new APIs in Javadoc
category: feature
requirement: '## Context


  Recent public Jenkins APIs were added with placeholder or inaccurate version markers, which makes it harder for plugin developers to know when they can rely on them.


  ## Desired outcome


  The Javadoc for the newly introduced APIs should report the correct released version without changing runtime behavior.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The affected public APIs keep the same names and semantics, but their `@since` documentation points to the correct release.

  '
=========== jenkins-load-view-recovery.yaml ===========
title: Recover views after error in `Jenkins.load`
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator reloading configuration from disk expects a failed reload to leave the current view layout intact, but an exception during unmarshal can corrupt the in-memory view list and even leave `primaryView` in a broken recursive state.


  ## Desired outcome

  If configuration reload fails partway through, Jenkins should restore the original `views` collection and `primaryView` before rethrowing the error so the running controller remains navigable. Administrators should get the reload failure, but not lose access to their existing view configuration because of that failed attempt.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A reload failure does not wipe or corrupt the current view list, `primaryView` is restored to the pre-reload value instead of remaining null or recursive, and the controller stays usable after the failed reload while still surfacing the original error.

  '
=========== jetty-12-ee8-upgrade.yaml ===========
title: '[JENKINS-73130] Upgrade core from Jetty 10.x to 12.x (EE 8)'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context


  Jenkins needs the Jetty 12 EE8 upgrade to stay on supported infrastructure, but operators and plugin developers cannot absorb a server upgrade that silently breaks uploads, WebSocket settings, or existing compatibility knobs.


  ## Desired outcome


  The runtime should move to Jetty 12 EE8 while preserving established Jenkins behavior and keeping existing multipart tuning properties usable during the transition.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The WebSocket provider honors `jenkins.websocket.idleTimeout`, non-WebSocket requests are still rejected cleanly, and the legacy multipart property names `RequestImpl.FILEUPLOAD_MAX_FILES`, `RequestImpl.FILEUPLOAD_MAX_FILE_SIZE`, and `RequestImpl.FILEUPLOAD_MAX_SIZE` continue to map to the new `MultipartFormDataParser` limits.

  '
=========== keyboard-scroll-selection.yaml ===========
title: Fix scrolling with keyboard
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins user navigating Command Palette results with the keyboard expects arrow-key movement to keep the selected item visible, but the current scroll helper can miss cases where the selected element is undefined and keyboard navigation becomes unreliable.


  ## Desired outcome

  Keyboard-driven navigation should tolerate the absence of a selected item and only try to scroll when a real selection exists. The Command Palette should continue to wire keyboard handling only while it is open so arrow-key navigation stays smooth instead of tripping over an uninitialized selection.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Using the keyboard to move through Command Palette results no longer throws or stalls when nothing is selected yet, scrolling resumes once an item is actually selected, and navigation remains scoped to the palette while it is open.

  '
=========== lifecycle-boot-failure.yaml ===========
title: '`Lifecycle.onBootFailure`'
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  Alternate Jenkins lifecycle implementations can react to restart and shutdown events, but they are not told when the controller fails during boot.


  ## Desired outcome


  Lifecycle providers should receive an explicit boot-failure callback so environments that rely on process supervision or auto-restart can handle startup failures intentionally.


  ## Acceptance signals


  A failed startup calls `Lifecycle.onBootFailure(BootFailure)`, and lifecycles such as the exit-based implementation can respond by restarting or terminating according to their policy.

  '
=========== lts-24793-zip-installer.yaml ===========
title: Backporting for 2.479.3 LTS (part 3)
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  ## Desired outcome

  ## Acceptance signals

  Valid non-HTTP(S) URIs that resolve through `Path.of(uri)` are accepted, malformed non-HTTP(S) values still fail validation, and zip-based tool installers using local URIs work again on the backported line.

  '
=========== makebutton-jenkins-button.yaml ===========

category: ci

  '
=========== manage-monitor-visibility.yaml ===========
title: Allow administrative monitors to be displayed for users with `Overall/MANAGE` permission
category: other

  '
=========== modernize-build-trend-page.yaml ===========
title: modernise build time trend page
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  '
=========== nodelistener-oncreated-initialization.yaml ===========
title: Ensure NodeListener#onCreated is called once the Node initialization is complete
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Plugin developers using `NodeListener#onCreated` expect the callback to run only after the new node is fully initialized, because creation handlers may immediately read filesystem-backed node state. Jenkins currently fires the event too early for that contract to be safe.


  ## Desired outcome

  ## Acceptance signals

  `NodeListener#onCreated` fires only after the node has been inserted and loaded, listeners can safely touch initialization-dependent state like `node.getRootDir()` during creation handling, and plugins no longer need to defer basic created-node work to avoid premature callbacks.

  '

category: bugfix

  '
=========== offline-api-since-annotations.yaml ===========
title: Fill in since annotations
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Jenkins core and plugin maintainers rely on `@since` metadata to understand when public offline-state APIs became available, especially when adopting newer agent-state contracts across weekly and LTS lines. Missing version tags make those contracts harder to use safely.


  ## Desired outcome

  The public offline-state APIs introduced with the newer computer model should advertise accurate availability information, including `Computer.setOfflineCause(OfflineCause)`, `IOfflineCause`, and `IComputer.getOfflineCause()` as available since `2.483`.   ## Acceptance signals

  '
=========== offline-by-design-ui.yaml ===========
title: Display appropriate GUI that accurately displays offline by design
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator looking at an agent that is offline by design needs the UI to distinguish between an intentional pause, a user-requested temporary disconnect, and a genuinely offline machine, but the current computer pages and exported state collapse those cases into the wrong icons and messages.


  ## Desired outcome

  Computers that are offline because they are intentionally not accepting tasks should expose that state through the newer `IComputer` and `IOfflineCause` contracts, including the ability to set an offline reason on a never-connected computer with `setOfflineCause(OfflineCause cause)`. The UI and exported search data should then show the correct iconography and reason text for user-disconnected agents versus agents that are simply offline by design.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Agents that are paused or not accepting tasks show distinct visual treatment from disconnected agents, `IComputer.getOfflineCause()` and `IOfflineCause` provide the offline-by-design details needed by the UI, and administrators no longer see a never-connected or intentionally paused agent presented as if it had unexpectedly gone offline.

  '
=========== offline-status-persistence.yaml ===========
title: '[JENKINS-30101][JENKINS-30175] Simplify persistence design for temporarily offline status'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context


  The temporary offline state for an agent currently lives partly on the `Computer`, which makes the status fragile across reconnects, controller restarts, and node reconfiguration even though operators expect that intent to persist with the node itself.


  ## Desired outcome


  Temporary offline state and its message should be owned by the `Node`, while compatibility entry points on `Computer` and the CLI continue to behave as operators expect.


  ## Acceptance signals


  Taking an agent offline through the CLI records an `OfflineCause.ByCLI`, `getTemporaryOfflineCauseReason()` reports the persisted message, existing compatibility setters still work, and a missing target still reports `ERROR: No such agent "never_created" exists.`.

  '
=========== os-eol-warning-date.yaml ===========
title: '[JENKINS-73845] Fix OperatingSystemEndOfLifeAdminMonitor endOfLifeDate displayed on first warning day'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator who sees the operating-system end-of-life warning on the very first day it should appear expects the banner to report the real end-of-life date immediately, but the monitor can show the wrong value on that first warning day.


  ## Desired outcome

  `OperatingSystemEndOfLifeAdminMonitor` should activate on the first warning day and expose `getEndOfLifeDate()` as the actual configured end-of-life date for the matched operating system, not a placeholder or later-updated value. Administrators should be able to trust the date shown in the warning as soon as the banner first appears.


  ## Acceptance signals

  On the warning start date, the monitor activates for the matching OS, `getEndOfLifeDate()` returns the configured end-of-life date right away, and the banner shows the same date administrators are expected to plan around.

  '
=========== peepholepermalink-cache-extension.yaml ===========
title: '`PeepholePermalink.Cache`'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Plugin developers who customize permalink lookup need a supported way to replace the cache behind `PeepholePermalink`, and Jenkins operators expect nearest-build navigation to keep returning the correct build around gaps created by deleted runs. The current implementation hard-codes the cache and leaves some lookup semantics implicit.


  ## Desired outcome

  `PeepholePermalink` should expose its cache as an extension point through `PeepholePermalink.Cache`, with persisted entries using the existing `id + " " + (build == null ? -1 : build.getNumber())` storage shape so alternate cache implementations remain compatible. At the same time, nearest-build and nearest-old-build resolution should preserve the exact numeric behavior Jenkins expects when build numbers are missing.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Plugins can supply a `PeepholePermalink.Cache` implementation without replacing permalink logic wholesale, persisted cache entries stay compatible with the `id + " " + (build == null ? -1 : build.getNumber())` format, and nearest-build navigation returns the documented builds before and after gaps caused by deletions.

  '
